question.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4t⟩,$ use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of $t.$ 

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k.$*
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are told that

$$
{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(12\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-9)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+81} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{15}{{5}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
